name: Coasters: Fourth Dimension 1.5.0
changelog:
# Coasters: Fourth Dimension 1.5.0

For **Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.256 and Java 21**. Install matching Fourth Dimension builds on clients and servers.

## New in this release

- Eight native moving-track mechanisms: transfer platform, turntable, drop track, tilt track, elevator, teeter-totter, side-drop and simultaneous yaw/pitch table.
- Original machinery, recipes, paid Survival construction, swept-clearance preview, compatibility guidance and guarded operator controls.
- Physical whole-train retention, exclusive destination reservations, locked docking, interrupted recovery and occupied cold restoration.
- Includes the accepted 1.1 builder/operator tools, 1.2 fixed Arrow multi-train circuit, 1.3 model repairs/selectable bodies, and 1.4 Standing Standard/Surf, Motorbike and Flying Bike: **21 FD vehicle configurations** in total.
- Bounded fixed-span Powered, Magnetized and Engineered handoffs, plus four-car PAX full-turn recovery to its original winch station.

## Required stack

- [Create 6.0.10](https://modrinth.com/mod/create/version/UjX6dr61)
- [Create: Coasters Simulated 0.1.5](https://modrinth.com/mod/create-coasters-simulated/version/PGhQoSBq) — 0.1.6 is not part of this qualified stack.
- [Sable 2.0.6](https://modrinth.com/mod/sable/version/fg9dTRz9), which includes Sable Companion 1.6.0 and Veil 4.3.2.
- [Veil 4.3.2](https://modrinth.com/mod/veil/version/EcZhFl38) is required on clients and already included by the pinned Sable distribution. Do not replace it with a newer standalone Veil.
- Use Create's matching Flywheel/Ponder/Registrate support stack. Fourth Dimension does not bundle upstream mods.

Optional relations are linked directly wherever a verified platform project exists; the remaining addons retain CurseForge links here.

## Upgrade and operating limits

Back up existing worlds and test upgrades on a copy. Saves write schema9; matching client/server builds are required. Do not downgrade upgraded saves in place. Repairing a fault does not restart motion automatically; use explicit recovery.

Moving beds are straight 16/32/48-block assemblies with at most four homogeneous whole-consist cars, subject to each family's smaller limits and exact compatibility. Some families support only level-deck motion. Ordinary native service carts must be empty. Arbitrary contraptions, CTNB moving-bed materials, managed 1.2 dynamic routes and Launch Systems moving-track ownership are excluded.

At maximum size, synchronous geometry validation can pause the server; the observed worst transition was approximately **3.125 seconds**. Capacity is not a smoothness or FPS guarantee. The measured workload and physical stopping/derivative limits are retained in the acceptance record.

[Moving-track guide](https://github.com/StonyTark1117/Coasters-Fourth-Dimension/blob/v1.5.0/docs/MOVING-TRACK.md) · [All vehicle guides](https://github.com/StonyTark1117/Coasters-Fourth-Dimension/tree/v1.5.0#vehicles-and-guides) · [Acceptance and measurements](https://github.com/StonyTark1117/Coasters-Fourth-Dimension/blob/v1.5.0/docs/evidence/1.5/integration.md)

Validated with 75 unit tests and cumulative targeted native/occupied cases. The release JAR differs from the accepted checkpoint only in version/description metadata; all gameplay code and assets are identical. Independent Java21 builds are byte-identical.
